scenes.say: From twenty twenty-seven, Formula One broadcasts will show drivers' heart rates live in the race.
Formula One has signed a four-year deal with WHOOP. It was announced in Vegas.
It's the first consumer wearable the FIA has approved for racing. It sits on the upper arm, under a fireproof sleeve.
In a race a driver's heart averages more than one hundred and seventy beats a minute.
Not everyone is in. Verstappen said no: people don't need to know his heart rate.
Leclerc already wears the strap and has nothing to hide. And WHOOP has partnered Ferrari since January.
If Formula One opens up this data, we'll add it to LapRadar.

title: Driver heart rates on TV: F1 signs WHOOP, Verstappen opts out
